_comment:
Farm submission for the RG-D pi0 Stage A skim, target Cu. Dry-run:
  python -m pi0.batch config/farm/v022/Cu.farm.json
Submit:
  python -m pi0.batch config/farm/v022/Cu.farm.json --submit
Then, once every Stage A job is done:
  python -m pi0.batch config/farm/v022/Cu.farm.json --stage b

THIS FILE DOES NOT CARRY CUT VALUES. Every threshold lives in config/cuts.json and the run lists in config/runs.json; this file says only WHERE the data is and WHAT RESOURCES to ask for. A cut value appearing here is a bug. CU AND SN READ THE SAME INPUT FILES. They are two foils in one assembly exposed in the same CuSn runs and separated offline by the electron vz window (note sec:vertex), so this config and Sn.farm.json point at the identical /mss tree and differ ONLY in `target`. Submitting both means skimming the CuSn runs twice -- that is not a mistake to optimise away: the two vz windows select DISJOINT event sets, so the expensive part (GBT photon scoring, which runs only for events whose electron already passed) is not duplicated. Only the HIPO decode is.
_runlist_comment: target Cu -> run list CuSn. pi0.farm REFUSES any input file whose run is not in the outbending CuSn list of config/runs.json. THIS IS NOT DECORATION: the /mss tree below holds INBENDING runs alongside outbending ones (LD2 inbending is 18305-18336, outbending starts at 18419), and the slim schema does not record polarity -- so a plain recursive scan mixes torus polarities into one dataset and nothing downstream can notice. The note (tab:runs) records that the original run lists were 'not applied by any binary'; this key is what applies them.

farm._polarity_comment: Outbending only -- the production. The inbending set is the detector-systematic cross-check the analysis lacks entirely (note sec:outlook); running it means flipping this key, and the run-list filter then selects the right files by itself.
farm._inputs_comment: v0.2.2 production: the NEW SIDIS train (lower-case train/sidis/, one file per run, prescaled 1 in 5 for Q2 < 2.0 GeV2), not the 10% skim train/SIDIS/ of v0.2.1. A directory is scanned recursively for *.hipo; a glob or a literal file also work. /mss is tape -- SWIF2 stages each -input from tape to the node before the job runs. Use the /cache mirror instead if the files are already there. On a login node prefer `--file-list <list.dat>`: scanning 30k tape paths is slow, and the list is then a record of exactly what the production consumed.
farm._files_per_job_comment: 1, matching clas-framework's scripts/swif2_pi0_skim.py -- the submitter that actually ran this skim, whose defaults are files-per-job 1, cores 1, ram 4G, disk 20G, time 4h. THE TIME LIMIT IS CALIBRATED PER FILE: raising files_per_job without raising `time` in step gives jobs that are killed at the limit. (clas-framework's general pi0.farm.toml pairs files_per_job 5 with time 16:00:00 -- the same ratio, roughly.) stageA_skim takes ONE HIPO file per invocation regardless (it exits 5 on a multi-run file), so a chunk >1 just means the job wrapper loops and writes slim_0..slim_N-1.root. Chunks never span runs.
farm._skip_foreign_run_runs_comment: Runs whose file is skimmed with stageA_skim --skip-foreign-run --run <run> (new in v0.2.3): events of any other run are dropped, the rest of the run is kept. Run 19102 (since v0.2.8): its SIDIS-train file holds 2 events of run 19101 next to 11721840 events of 19102 (Stage A exit 5 in the v022 part1 production, 2026-11-15); the 2 events are dropped, every event of 19102 is kept. Run 18753 (since v1.0.0): its train file holds 2 events of run 18752 next to 11989466 events of 18753 (Stage A exit 5 in the v022 part2 production, 2026-11-16); the part2 job 105 was retried with --skip-foreign-run --run 18753, and this entry records that. Any other run is skimmed as before. If another run turns out to hold events of a second run, Stage A exits 5 for it; add the run here and resubmit that run only.
farm._exclude_runs_comment: Runs to drop from the run list, with a stated reason, e.g. a known bad run. Empty means the run list is taken as-is. runs.json records special_DC_runs_CuSn (18358-18368) but those are inbending and are not in the outbending list anyway.
farm._output_comment: Slims land at <output_dir>/<run>/<job>/slim_<i>.root and logs at <log_dir>/<job>.log. SWIF2's -output does NOT create the parent directory, so the generated script mkdir -p's each one; without that the copy back is simply lost.

swif2._cores_comment: stageA_skim is single-threaded (RHipoDS + a serial selection chain). Asking for more cores buys nothing and makes the job harder to schedule.
swif2._disk_comment: Must hold files_per_job staged HIPO DSTs plus their slims. A DST chunk is a few GB; the slim is ~100x smaller, so the staged inputs dominate.
swif2._time_comment: Converted to SWIF2's seconds form (14400s) at synthesis. Budget ~20% over single-file wall clock x files_per_job. A malformed value is refused at parse time here, not by the scheduler after you have submitted.
swif2._modules_comment: An OBJECT with a `load` array, not a bare array -- a bare array parses fine and silently loads nothing, and a node without ROOT fails at runtime, not at submit.

farm._env_comment: Exported in the job wrapper before the skim runs. Child of `farm`, NOT of `farm.swif2` -- this mirrors clas-framework, where the value is read from the farm table even though it is stored on the swif2 struct.
